title: Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors: index browser, schema and errors for custom connectors in the admin centre
summary: Hold: the checklist tells administrators to use Copilot Visibility to contain exposure from custom connectors, although the documentation establishes that control only for partner connectors. The Graph role-assignment guidance also omits the delegated-access qualification on its administrator-role requirement. The roadmap facts and the documented diagnostic views are supported.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans index browser, schema and error views for custom connectors in the Microsoft 365 admin center for troubleshooting.
claims.quote: View index browser, schema, and the errors for custom connectors from the M365 Admin center for better troubleshooting.

claims.claim: Microsoft's connector pages require AI administrator to access and manage connector pages.
claims.quote: To access and manage your Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors, you must be an AI administrator for your tenant.

claims.claim: AI Administrator is a privileged Microsoft Entra role.
claims.quote: This is a privileged role. Assign the AI Administrator role to users who need to do the following tasks:

claims.claim: AI Administrator manages all aspects of Microsoft Copilot, beyond connector troubleshooting.
claims.quote: Manage all aspects of Microsoft Copilot

claims.claim: AI Administrator assignments can be managed in Microsoft 365 admin center through Roles > Role assignments > Microsoft Entra ID > AI Administrator > Assigned > Add users.
claims.quote: go to Roles > Role assignments. ... choose the Microsoft Entra ID ... tab. ... Select the administrator role that you want to assign the user to. ... On the Assigned tab, select Add users or Add groups.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments creates a Microsoft Entra directory role assignment.
claims.quote: Create a role assignment for the directory provider: POST /roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments

claims.claim: The role-assignment request body sets roleDefinitionId.
claims.quote: The following example shows a request. Note the use of the roleTemplateId for roleDefinitionId. roleDefinitionId can be either the service-wide template Id or the directory-specific roleDefinitionId.

claims.claim: The role-assignment request body sets principalId.
claims.quote: principalId | String | Required. Identifier of the principal to which the assignment is granted.

claims.claim: Creating a role assignment through Microsoft Graph needs Privileged Role Administrator as the least privileged role, without an access-mode qualification.
claims.quote: Application | RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory ... For delegated access using work or school accounts, the signed-in user must be assigned a supported Microsoft Entra role ... Privileged Role Administrator is the least privileged role supported for this operation.
claims.fix: In the row note and Governance controls, replace the role sentence with: 'For delegated access using a work or school account, Privileged Role Administrator is the least privileged supported built-in role for this operation.' Keep the Graph call unchanged. Reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/rbacapplication-post-roleassignments?view=graph-rest-1.0.

claims.claim: The error-monitoring path is Microsoft 365 admin center > Connectors > Your connections > connection > Error.
claims.quote: To monitor errors, go to Connectors > Your connections in the Microsoft 365 admin center, select the connection, and choose Error in the connection details pane.

claims.claim: For the documented partner-connector control, the path is Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections > connection > Copilot Visibility in Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Go to Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections. Select the connection that you want to modify. Under Copilot Visibility, select the toggle to turn the connector on or off, and choose Save.

claims.claim: No automation operation is documented for the Copilot Visibility toggle.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot connectors Copilot Visibility toggle Microsoft Graph API externalConnection enabledContentExperiences'. Read manage-connector, externalConnection beta, Update connection beta and manage-connections; no operation documents this toggle's agent-exempt semantics.

claims.claim: Microsoft describes Copilot Visibility for partner connectors, without establishing its availability for API-built custom synced connectors.
claims.quote: Manage visibility of partner data sources in Copilot ... Admins can control the visibility of partner connectors in Copilot and Copilot Search via a simple toggle.

claims.claim: For documented partner connectors, switching visibility off excludes the connector from Copilot Search and Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: When the visibility is off, the connector is excluded from all Copilot Search and Copilot Chat results and responses.

claims.claim: The documented partner-connector visibility control is visible by default.
claims.quote: The default behavior is visible by default

claims.claim: Copilot Visibility does not affect declarative agents and their data.
claims.quote: with changes syncing automatically with search, without affecting declarative agents and their data.

claims.claim: Turning visibility off does not stop the connection from crawling its data source.
claims.quote: If the connection is off, it can still crawl the data source, but the data isn't used for search results.

claims.claim: Visibility changes can take up to 30 minutes to propagate across Copilot experiences.
claims.quote: After you update the visibility settings at the connection level, allow up to 30 minutes for the changes to propagate across all Copilot experiences.

claims.claim: Microsoft says updating a connection's configured access permissions after creation is not currently supported.
claims.quote: Updating access permissions after you create the connection isn't currently supported.

claims.claim: Microsoft's documented correction for unintended connection access permissions is to delete and recreate the connection with the intended permissions.
claims.quote: In the connector pane, choose Delete to delete the existing connection. Recreate the connection using the Custom setup flow and explicitly configure access permissions.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Changes to user or group ACL permissions can take up to 24 hours to appear in Microsoft Search and Microsoft 365 Copilot.
claims.quote: Changes to user or group permissions (ACLs) might take up to 24 hours to reflect in Microsoft Search and Microsoft 365 Copilot.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Permission updates occur during a full crawl rather than an incremental crawl, so a check immediately after a source change can show old permissions.
claims.quote: Permissions updates occur during a full crawl, not an incremental crawl. If your data source permissions change after the last full crawl, you must trigger a new full crawl on-demand or schedule it to update the index.

claims.claim: Federated connectors do not index content, so indexed-item lookup concerns synced connections.
